title: Logs
subtitle: Kernel buffer, journalctl, and classic /var/log files — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Print the kernel message ring buffer (boot, drivers, OOM, hardware events)
cards.notes: Not the same as /var/log/messages — size-limited kernel diary. First stop for “did the kernel see this device?”

cards.meaning: Kernel messages with human-readable wall-clock timestamps
cards.notes: Default dmesg often shows seconds since boot; -T is easier to correlate with other logs.

cards.meaning: Service that collects and stores structured, indexed binary journals from many sources
cards.notes: Centralizes kernel, unit stdout/stderr, syslog, audit, etc. Journals are binary — query with journalctl.

cards.meaning: Query and display systemd journal data
cards.notes: Cannot tail the journal files as plain text; always go through journalctl (or -f to follow).

cards.meaning: Show journal lines for that systemd unit only
cards.notes: -u filters by unit (service). Use when a service fails to start or misbehaves.

cards.meaning: Error and worse, this boot only, with extra explanatory help texts when available
cards.notes: -p priority · -b last boot (-b -1 previous) · -x adds context/hints when systemd has them.

cards.meaning: Filter by syslog identifier (not necessarily the unit name)
cards.notes: Same process can appear as -u docker.service and as -t dockerd. Use -t for the syslog id.

cards.meaning: Limit journal output to a time window (relative or absolute)
cards.notes: Phrases like "2 days ago" or "2015-06-26 23:15:00". Combine with -u, -p, -t.

cards.meaning: Global system text log including startup; mail, cron, daemon, kern, auth, …
cards.notes: Classic rsyslog file on RHEL-family. Debian/Ubuntu often uses /var/log/syslog instead.

cards.meaning: Authentication and authorization; sshd including failed logins (RHEL-family)
cards.notes: Who tried to log in and whether they succeeded. Pair with journalctl -u sshd when using the journal.

cards.meaning: System authorization, user logins, and auth mechanisms (Debian-family)
cards.notes: Same story as /var/log/secure on RHEL — know which file your distro uses.

cards.meaning: Cron/anacron job start and related scheduling log lines
cards.notes: Check here when a scheduled job “didn’t run” or ran at the wrong time.

cards.meaning: Mail server log (e.g. sendmail); /var/log/mail/ holds extra mail logs
cards.notes: Name varies by distro: maillog vs mail.log. Subdirectory /var/log/mail/ for more detail.

cards.meaning: Daily sar data files collected by the sysstat package
cards.notes: Historical CPU/IO stats that sar reads. Memory hook: sa/ = sysstat archive.

cards.front: boot/hardware vs unit vs classic files
cards.meaning: dmesg for kernel; journalctl for systemd units; /var/log/… for classic syslog text
cards.notes: Pick the source that matches the failure class — don’t grep everywhere first.
